To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

an 18T structural variant within the gene SCAF4, which is located adjacent to the SOD1 locus, is associated with fALS in a North American cohort, and that carriage of this allele is associated with a 25% reduction in survival time.

a 3' untranslated structural polymorphism in the SCAF4 gene is associated with disease in a predominantly Sod1 fALS cohort, and that the 18T allele is associated with a 6-month increase in age at onset and a 2-year decrease in survival.

a 12-18T repeat in the 3' UTR of SCAF4, a gene that is located next to SOD1 and is involved in mRNA processing, is associated with disease susceptibility in a predominantly Sod1 fALS cohort, and that the presence of an 18-T repeat is associated with reduced survival time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel structural variant within SCAF4 that may influence disease susceptibility and survival in patients with fALS, and may have broader relevance to ALS pathophysiology.
a genetic variant in a gene that has not been previously associated with fALS or sporadic ALS (sALS).
the identification of genetic factors associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 18T structural variant in the SCAF4 gene is associated with a 6.6-fold increase in ALS risk in a predominantly Sod1 fALS cohort.
rs573116163 is associated with disease in fALS, but not in sporadic ALS.
the SCAF4 variant is not a disease-causing variant in SOD1-ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a SCAF4 structural variant, rs573116164, has disease-modifying effects on fALS.
the 18T SCAFF4 variant is associated with fALS and has an effect on survival, but not on age at onset.
the 18T allele of rs573116164 is associated with fALS, and that the 18 T allele is associated with reduced survival in SOD1 fAALS patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 12-18 repeat polymorphism in SCAF4, a gene that is located next to SOD1 and is known to interact with SOD1 in the cell, has a disease-modifying effect in fALS.
the 18T allele in SCAF4 is associated with a 6-fold increased risk of developing fALS in the SOD1 population, but also in the non-SOD1 population, suggesting a broader relevance in the disease.
a 12-18 T repeat in SCAF4 is associated with fALS, and that this association is SOD1-independent.
